questions.answer: Shelter (if on the country) stops it automatically; otherwise spend the hardening token, or your own ambassador on the hex, or Aegis Doctrine (drones at bases don't help in war). gaps: Does an adversary troop landing (Muster) on a hex with an ambassador cancel it one for one, as an agent does? Only agents are covered.

Solo: must I keep all 4 drafted cards (and pay), or may I discard some as in multiplayer?
A threat with two tokens that places pieces: which token do they go on?
'Unity taken back' on event cards: how is it taken (Unity track only? can it go below 0 or undo a tip)?
The §21 table: is compute income really 4 at level 1 and 22 at level 2, and is agent income at level 0 really 1 including Garrisons (base 0)?
How a shield (hardening token on a node hex) gets onto a hex with only a node, when Harden and Bulwark target stations and factories.
overall: A careful, well-ordered rulebook: the round table, the near/nearest split and the worked examples (corruption, march, tipping) let me answer almost every question with confidence. The cost is density: many paragraphs carry a parenthetical exception (Wall's production exception, step 6's Muster exceptions, marker rules, per-tag gains on events) that I had to reread, and a few rules appear only in Part 2 (agents moving off adversary sites). The biggest gaps are around ambassadors: whether troops cancel them on landing, where spent ones go, and whether a shared hardening token can be held back. The difficulty table's compute jump and the solo keep wording look like they need a second look.
